newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET- AZHARUDDIN SENDS S.AFRICA ON BIG RUN HUNT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET- AZHARUDDIN SENDS S.AFRICA ON BIG RUN HUNT.

text.p: Mohammed Azharuddin's unbeaten 163 helped India declare their second innings at 400 for seven and set South Africa a 461-run victory target on the fourth day of their third and final cricket test on Wednesday.
Azharuddin's 16th century in 75 tests strengthened India, who led by 60 runs in the first innings after South Africa were all out for 177 in reply to India's 237.
India, overnight 270 for five, declared at their lunch-time score after Azharuddin, 88 overnight, struck 25 boundaries and on-drove off-spinner Pat Symcox for a six in his 312-minute, 288-ball knock.

Azharuddin and Rahul Dravid took their sixth-wicket stand to 165 runs, the highest Indian stand for any wicket against South Africa, before left-arm spinner Paul Adams had Dravid caught by Brian McMillan at slip for 56.
Adams, who has claimed two wickets for 84, bowled left-hander Sunil Joshi for 16 as the seventh Indian wicket fell at 385.
